acs.text: When a submission is withdrawn, the package's remaining seat count on `/publish` increases by exactly one.

expected_answer.baseline: package remaining seat count on `/publish` before the withdrawal

acs.text: `/my-submissions` only shows submissions created in the current browser session.

expected_answer.operand: a submission created in a different browser session appears in the current browser session's `/my-submissions` view

acs.text: When `/my-submissions` shows submission rows, the header `My Submissions (N)` count equals the number of rows in the table.

operand.derived: number of submission rows shown in the `/my-submissions` table

acs.text: After a submission is withdrawn from `/my-submissions`, that submission row is no longer shown in the table.

expected_answer.operand: the withdrawn submission row remains visible in the `/my-submissions` table after withdrawal

acs.text: Each submission row shown on `/my-submissions` offers a `Withdraw` control.

expected_answer.operand: each submission row in the `/my-submissions` table exposes a `Withdraw` control

acs.text: A newly created submission is shown with the status `Under Review`.
When the current browser session has at least one submission, `/my-submissions` shows a table with the columns Reference, Book Title, Author, Package, Seat and Status.

expected_answer.operand: table columns Reference, Book Title, Author, Package, Seat and Status

acs.text: When the current browser session has no submissions, `/my-submissions` shows `You haven't submitted a manuscript yet.`.

expected_answer.operand: text `You haven't submitted a manuscript yet.` is shown on `/my-submissions`

acs.text: When the current browser session has no submissions, `/my-submissions` shows a link to browse packages.

expected_answer.operand: a link to browse packages is shown on `/my-submissions`

judgements.rationale: No source evidence introduced money handling, authentication, or destructive data loss for this use-case. The main risks were shared seat capacity visible to all visitors, browser-session scoping, and display consistency on a user-facing page.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because seat restoration affects the shared monthly pool for every visitor and can regress when submission or package availability logic changes.

Applied user-reach and change-frequency because browser-session isolation determines which submissions a visitor can see and is coupled to session-storage behavior called out explicitly in the source.
Applied user-reach because a mismatched header count misstates the user's current submissions, but it does not directly alter shared capacity.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because withdrawal behavior changes visible state immediately and depends on the same mutable submission state as the shared seat pool.
Applied user-reach because the withdraw affordance is user-facing and required for self-serve reversal, with lower system impact than pool accounting.
Applied user-reach because the initial status is visible to the author and can affect their understanding of the submission state.
Applied user-reach because the table structure is a visible reporting promise for authors reviewing their submissions.
Applied user-reach because the empty-state message is directly visible when a session has no submissions.
Applied user-reach because the browse-packages link directs the author's recovery path from the empty state.
